Class ClausifierExpr

java.lang.Object
com.articulate.sigma.parsing.ClausifierExpr
public class ClausifierExpr extends Object
Pure Expr → Expr CNF clausification pipeline.

This is the Expr-based counterpart of {com.articulate.sigma.Clausifier}. Every step is a stateless static method; the only mutable state is the int[] counter(s) threaded through the call tree for generating unique names.

Pipeline (mirrors the string-based Clausifier):

  1. equivalencesOut(Expr) — eliminate <=>
  2. implicationsOut(Expr) — eliminate =>
  3. negationsIn(Expr) — push not to narrowest scope (NNF)
  4. renameVariables(Expr, int[]) — give each variable a unique name
  5. existentialsOut(Expr, int[]) — Skolemize existential quantifiers
  6. universalsOut(Expr) — drop forall wrappers
  7. disjunctionsIn(Expr) — distribute or over and
  8. standardizeApart(Expr, int[]) — rename vars per clause

    • renameVariables

      public static Expr renameVariables(Expr expr, int[] varIdx)
      Rename all variables (Var and RowVar) to unique names. Implicitly universally quantified variables (appearing free at the top level) are renamed consistently; each explicitly quantified variable gets a fresh name scoped to its quantifier.
      Parameters:
      varIdx - A single-element array used as a mutable counter; it is updated in place so the same array can be reused across subsequent steps that also need fresh names.

    • toNegAndPosLitsWithRenameInfo

      public static List toNegAndPosLitsWithRenameInfo(Formula f)
      Convert a {Formula} to the three-element clausal-form list expected by {link Formula#getTheClausalForm()}.

      The returned list contains:

      1. A List<List<List<Formula>>> — clauses; each clause is a two-element list [negLits, posLits].
      2. The original {link Formula} input.
      3. An empty Map<String,String> — rename tracking is not exposed by the Expr pipeline; the map is empty but structurally present so callers using index-2 access ({link Formula#getVarMap()}) receive an empty map rather than an exception.
